content.text: No audit, inspection, or usage-verification right running against the Client exists anywhere in the agreement. The only verification mechanic runs in our favour (§ 6, Client entitled to supporting documentation and to contest charges), and § 8's Client covenants contain no audit obligation. Absence of any Vendor audit right is better than the preferred position, so there is nothing to limit and nothing to flag.

input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: Searches for audit, inspection, records, books, verification, examination, premises, monitoring and usage rights return no provision granting TrueLink any right to audit, inspect or verify Client's usage, records or systems. Section 5 (Compensation) and Section 6 contain only a one-way verification right in our favour — Client may request documentation supporting charges and contest them — and Section 8 (Client covenants) imposes no audit obligation on Client; the only Client-side access obligation (p0060) is to let TrueLink perform Y2K repairs at TrueLink's sole cost, not to permit an audit. Because TrueLink has no audit right at all, the agreement is better than the preferred position (no frequency, notice, cost or system-access limits are needed), and the absence benefits our party, so no redline is warranted.
